weave-lines.note: At 1280 and 390, on ink and paper, the field reads as cloth and not as a net: short horizontal and vertical ribbon bars alternate over and under along every row and column, each ribbon shows two edge hairlines, and the 6px gutters stay open (ribbon 0.75 of a 24px pitch). The under strand's edges visibly stop before the over strand, so no edge is drawn through a crossing, and the field is clearly not hatch-lines, grid-paper or brick-lattice. At 390 the same 24px pitch is cut cleanly at the frame with no stub. At strength 0.35 the lines are faint on ink and slightly firmer on paper, and the headline and copy stay readable on both. The tile period is 2 times float times pitch, as briefed, and the path keeps whole-pixel runs on half-pixel lines. Not verified: pixel-level crispness and tile seams (a zoomed crop was refused in this session) and float 2 or 3, because only default captures exist. triangular-mesh.note: The revision landed. At 1280 on ink and paper there are four mint marks, inside the briefed three to five: about x 665 y 60, x 869 y 354, x 190 y 400 and x 486 y 599. They are spread across the top, the middle and the lower half, with none clustered and none under the heading or the copy line, which ends at x 465 and y 77, well clear of the nearest mark. The earlier cluster in the right middle is gone, and every mark is at least 40px from any frame edge. At 390 on both grounds a single mark sits at x 190 y 400, centred and clear of the text and the edges. The wireframe still reads distinctly: every face is a triangle of a different shape, no edges cross and no face looks flipped, there is a dot at each interior node, rows and columns stay legible under the jitter, and the mesh reaches all four sides at the same 48px spacing. The edges stay quiet under the heading on both grounds. The core now defaults marks to 1 and carries a 2px mark inset. The brief now says about three to five marks at the 1 percent default in a 1280 by 800 frame, and its prop line says default 1, so the code, the brief and the captures agree. Residual risk: the captures are 1x, so I cannot confirm the inset to the pixel; no mark comes near an edge in them. Marks are seed dependent, so a seed other than 1 may cluster or land on the copy, which is a user choice. Only default props were captured.

step-diagonals.note: At 1280 and 390 on both grounds the staircases are strictly horizontal and vertical, with equal 12px treads and risers at about 45 degrees, square corners, and channels four risers apart that are staircases themselves. No oblique stroke appears, so it is not diagonal-stripes, and the 390 frame is cut at the edge with no partial corner or stub. No gap or doubled corner shows where tiles meet at any captured size, and the lines look single-pixel and unblurred. The headline and copy stay readable at strength 0.3 on ink and paper; the paper capture is the firmer of the two. On the tile change: the builder was right and the brief was wrong. A staircase is invariant under a shift of one tread right and one riser up, not under a pure horizontal shift of one tread, so a tile run times step wide cannot repeat across without breaking the stair. The shipped tile is run times step times spacing wide by step times spacing tall, which is the smallest rectangle that repeats exactly, and the path is overdrawn a tread past each side so corners are whole. Change the brief, not the code: replace the tile size with run times step times spacing by step times spacing and say why. Not verified: a zoomed pixel check of the seams, which was refused in this session, and run 2 to 4 or the falling direction, since only default captures exist; the mirror transform with a half-pixel offset is the one place a blurred line could hide on falling.
